summary.text: Thomas Kean Jr. is the Republican incumbent for New Jersey's 7th Congressional District, first elected in 2022 after serving in the New Jersey General Assembly (2001-2003) and Senate (2003-2022), where he led the Republican caucus.

A son of former Gov. Thomas H. Kean, he previously worked at the Environmental Protection Agency and as a congressional staffer, and he sits on the House Energy and Commerce and Foreign Affairs committees.

paragraphs.text: Kean was born in Livingston, New Jersey, in 1968, the son of former New Jersey Gov. Thomas H. Kean, who served from 1982 to 1990.

He earned a bachelor's degree from Dartmouth College in 1990 and a master's degree in law and diplomacy from Tufts University's Fletcher School in 1997, where, according to his official biography, he was also employed as a graduate school instructor.

His career in public service began with an appointment by President George H.W. Bush to the Environmental Protection Agency, after which he worked in Washington, D.C., as a legislative staffer for U.S. Rep. Bob Franks.
Kean also volunteered as a firefighter and emergency medical technician and served as vice president of a fire department.

Kean was elected to the New Jersey General Assembly in 2001 and to the New Jersey Senate in 2003. He served in the Senate until 2022, including as Republican (minority) leader from 2008 to 2022, and his official biography lists service on the Senate Higher Education, Commerce, and Legislative Oversight committees.
He ran for the 7th District U.S. House seat in 2020 and lost to incumbent Democrat Tom Malinowski, then won the seat in 2022 by defeating Malinowski.

In the 119th Congress, Kean serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee (Health; Communications and Technology; and Commerce, Manufacturing and Trade subcommittees) and the Foreign Affairs Committee (Middle East and North Africa; South and Central Asia subcommittees). He is listed as a member of the Problem Solvers Caucus, Bipartisan Disabilities Caucus, and SALT Caucus.
According to his official biography, he lives in Westfield, New Jersey, with his wife Rhonda and their two daughters.
